reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that status no redline or counterparty comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to reject.

The cited text supports the compliance call: Section 13.5's disclaimer opens with 'EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII,' which preserves RevMed's express representations and warranties in Section 13.2, so the clause is the opposite of the rule's walk-away ('AS IS' with all warranties disclaimed).

Performance-standard and compliance-with-law elements of the rule are present in the cited paragraphs: Sections 4.2(b)/5.2(b) (p0291, p0313) require performance in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP/GLP/GCP plus diligent efforts against plan timelines, and Section 13.4(b) (p0572) adds a mutual compliance covenant — the industry-standard analogue of 'professional and workmanlike.'

The failed deterministic check (no 90-day/12-month period) is a phrasing/deal-type mismatch rather than evidence of a gap: this is a research, development and commercialization collaboration with no software or discrete deliverable, and batch-level conformance and acceptance remedies are expressly routed to the Supply and Quality Agreements under Section 7.3 (p0360).

Sub-elements short of the preferred wording (no fixed conformance-to-documentation period with an express repair/replace/refund election, no malicious-code warranty, Section 13.2 warranties given only as of the Execution Date) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than escalated to a deviation, per the playbook's classification semantics; the forward-looking follow-up on Supply/Quality Agreement conformance warranties is an appropriate tracking note, not a redline.

Minor observation only: parts of the rationale rely on paragraphs not supplied here (p0292, p0314, p0564, p0583), but the compliance conclusion is independently supported by the paragraphs that were provided.
